name: Medicalis - International Congress for Students and Young Doctors
audience: Medical students and junior doctors, 500+ per edition
timing: Annual, March. 26th edition ran 12-15 March 2026. Next window spring 2027 - watch the page from autumn 2026
why_relevant: Over 25 years old, hosted by UMF Iuliu Hatieganu, accredited, and its programme is built around practical workshops rather than lectures only. The audience is 18+ students with no diabetes - exactly the control arm the protocol needs 100 of
suggested_ask: Submit a 60-90 minute hands-on workshop: everyone plays a full Sugar-Sugar session on their own laptop or phone, then we put the room's MAE against the GlucoBench 60-minute figures on one slide. 3D-printed prize for the best predictor in the room
notes: Verified via UMF Cluj and Viata Medicala coverage 2026. No workshop-submission email found on the public pages - route through UMF Cluj student office or the Medicalis Facebook page

name: IMSCB - International Medical Students' Congress of Bucharest
audience: Medical students, international; biggest student congress in Romania
timing: Annual. Run by SSMB under UMFCD patronage - check imscbucharest.com/schedule for the next edition
why_relevant: Explicitly states it runs workshops, roundtables and a science fair and wants participants to build practical skills and critical thinking. A prediction game that ends in a measured error score is a critical-thinking exercise with a number at the end
suggested_ask: Propose a workshop plus a science-fair table: the workshop is the guided play, the table runs all day with a laptop, a leaderboard and the printed souvenirs
notes: Organised by SSMB (see ws-ssmb-zem) - one approach to SSMB can cover both. English-language congress, so Livia's English deck works unchanged

name: MEDIS - International Medical Congress for Students and Young Doctors of Timisoara
audience: Medical students and young doctors
timing: Annual, April. MEDIS26 ran 22-26 April 2026. Next window spring 2027
why_relevant: Timisoara is also where the 2026 national diabetes congress was held and where the UMFT diabetes department sits, so one trip can cover the student congress and the department
suggested_ask: Workshop proposal to the MEDIS organising team, paired with a guest-lecture request to the UMFT diabetes department in the same week
notes: Pair with ws-umft-diabet. Announced through the UMFT events page

name: MEDICIS - International Francophone Congress of Medicine and Dentistry for Students and Young Doctors
audience: 1500+ students and young doctors, 300+ lecturers from 20+ countries
timing: Annual, March. 2nd edition 25-29 March 2026. Next window spring 2027
why_relevant: The largest student audience found in Romania by headcount. The catch is the language: it is a francophone congress, and the study UI has French but our speaker does not present in French
suggested_ask: Only worth pursuing if a French-language session is realistic. Otherwise ask AMSFI (the organising association) to run the game as a corridor activity rather than a talk
notes: Organised by AMSFI with UMF Grigore T. Popa Iasi. Verified via news.umfiasi.ro 2026. Language is the blocker - record the decision before spending time here

name: KronMed - National Congress for Students and Young Doctors
audience: Medical students and young doctors
timing: Annual, March. 6th edition 27-29 March 2026. Next window spring 2027
why_relevant: Smaller and younger than Medicalis or IMSCB, which usually means an organising team that is easier to reach and more willing to take an unusual session
suggested_ask: Offer the workshop as a slot they can advertise: a browser game, no equipment needed, everyone leaves with a number and a printed object
notes: Smallest of the Romanian student congresses catalogued - good place to run the workshop for the first time before pitching the bigger ones

name: MedEspera - International Medical Congress for Students and Young Doctors
audience: Students, PhD students and young doctors; 74 workshops in the 2026 programme
timing: Biennial-to-annual, May. 11th edition 6-8 May 2026, theme "Building a New Era of Medicine with AI"
why_relevant: The 2026 theme was medicine and AI, the working language includes Romanian, and the programme carried 74 workshops - a congress that already schedules this format at scale. Moldova is a short trip and the audience is Romanian-speaking
suggested_ask: Email medespera@usmf.md asking how workshops are selected for the next edition, and propose the play-and-measure session under the AI theme
notes: The only row in this file with a published organiser email for workshops. Organised by USMF Nicolae Testemitanu with the Association of Medical Students and Residents of Moldova

name: Conferinta Nationala de Bioinginerie pentru Studenti si Tineri Cercetatori (BENG)
audience: Bioengineering students and young researchers
timing: Annual, May. 28th edition 6-10 May 2026, five days with a dedicated workshop track
why_relevant: Bioengineering students are the one Romanian student audience that can take both halves of the offer: play the study, and then sit through an honest lecture on time-series forecasting and why a human baseline matters for evaluating a model
suggested_ask: Propose the double bill - a play session plus the time-series ML lecture - to the Association of Bioengineering Students and the Faculty of Medical Bioengineering at UMF Grigore T. Popa
notes: Organised by the bioengineering student association under the Faculty of Medical Bioengineering, UMF Iasi. This is the best single fit in the file for the ML-teaching half of the offer

name: SSMB - Zilele Educatiei Medicale (Medical Education Days)
audience: ~700 medical students per edition, 63 events in 2026
timing: Annual, March. 19th edition 13-22 March 2026. Next window March 2027
why_relevant: Ten days of nothing but workshops, conferences and medical debates - a programme designed to absorb exactly the session we want to run, and the organiser also runs IMSCB
suggested_ask: One approach to SSMB covering both ZEM and IMSCB: a workshop slot in ZEM as the trial run, the IMSCB science fair as the follow-up
notes: Founded 1875, represents Faculty of Medicine students at UMF Carol Davila. Contact page at ssmb.ro/contact did not expose an address on fetch - get the email from the contact page or the partners page in a browser

name: FASMR - Federatia Asociatiilor Studentilor in Medicina din Romania
audience: Medical students across 8 Romanian university centres
timing: Year-round; national campaigns and general assemblies
why_relevant: The federation layer above the local societies. One agreement here reaches Bucharest, Cluj, Iasi, Timisoara, Targu Mures, Craiova, Constanta and Brasov instead of eight separate negotiations
suggested_ask: Ask FASMR to carry the workshop as a repeatable module its member associations can each book, rather than asking for one event
notes: Membership figures differ between public sources (over 10,000 in one, over 24,000 in another) - do not quote a number until it is verified. The current site is a placeholder shell on fetch; old.fasmr.ro carries the descriptive pages

name: Liga Studentilor din Targu Mures (FASMR member)
audience: Medical students in Targu Mures
timing: Academic year
why_relevant: A named local FASMR member with its own site, in the same city as ASCOTID - a single trip could do a student workshop and a patient-association session
suggested_ask: Offer the workshop as a student-society evening; ask in the same message whether they co-run anything with ASCOTID Mures
notes: Pair with the ascotid-ro row in diabetes-orgs-catalogue.csv

name: UMF Iuliu Hatieganu - Disciplina Diabet si Boli de Nutritie
audience: Medical students, residents, diabetology staff
contact: Prof. dr. Gabriela Roman - groman@umfcluj.ro, 0264594455; clinic 0264-296829
timing: Academic year; a guest lecture can be slotted into a clinical rotation any term
why_relevant: The department's own published research interests include technology and telemedicine in diabetes management. That is the nearest thing in Romania to a department whose stated agenda already contains what Sugar-Sugar measures
suggested_ask: Write to Prof. Roman: a guest lecture to the diabetology rotation, with the students playing the study during the session, and a question about whether the clinic's adult patients could be told the study exists
notes: Strongest named academic contact in this file: a public university email for the head of discipline. Address: Centrul Clinic de Diabet, str. Clinicilor 2-4, Cluj-Napoca. Professional contact details only - never record anything about any person's health

name: UMF Carol Davila - Disciplina Diabet, Nutritie si Boli Metabolice (Institutul N. Paulescu)
audience: Medical students, residents, diabetology staff
timing: Academic year
why_relevant: The largest diabetes teaching unit in Romania, attached to the N. Paulescu National Institute of Diabetes - the institutional centre of gravity for Romanian diabetology, and named after the man who isolated insulin
suggested_ask: Request a seminar slot for students, and separately ask the discipline whether the institute's outpatient adults may be told about the study
notes: Titular professors listed on the department page: Radulian Gabriela, Serafinceanu Cristian, Guja Cristian. No individual emails are published - the rectorate switchboard is the only listed route. Address: Str. Dionisie Lupu 37, Bucharest

name: UMF Victor Babes Timisoara - Department VII, Diabetes, Nutrition and Metabolic Diseases
audience: Medical students, residents, diabetology staff
timing: Academic year
why_relevant: Faculty listed on the department page include Prof. Romulus Timar, publicly reported as incoming president of SRDNBM, and Prof. Bogdan Timar. A lecture here is also an introduction to the national society
suggested_ask: Ask for a guest lecture to the diabetology rotation and, in the same message, for advice on getting a Sugar-Sugar workshop onto the SRDNBM congress programme
notes: Verify the SRDNBM presidency claim before using it in writing - it comes from a medichub.ro news item, not from the society's own site. Clinic founded 1973. Pair with ws-medis-timisoara and ws-srdnbm-congres

name: UMF Grigore T. Popa Iasi - diabetes teaching and the Iasi County Diabetes Clinical Centre
audience: Medical and nursing students, residents
timing: Academic year
why_relevant: Iasi carries both a diabetes teaching unit and the bioengineering faculty that runs BENG, so one visit can serve the clinical audience and the engineering audience
suggested_ask: Bundle with the BENG proposal: one trip, a clinical seminar and a student-conference workshop
notes: Named staff seen in public UMF Iasi documents - Mariana Graur (head of the county diabetes clinical centre) and Cristina Mihaela Lacatusu (named in a UMF Iasi teaching-post competition file). Both need confirming against a current department page before contact. Pair with ws-beng-iasi

name: UNST Politehnica Bucharest - Faculty of Medical Engineering
audience: Medical-engineering students, BSc and MSc
timing: Academic year; UPB also runs free ML/AI and data-science courses that carry time-series content
why_relevant: An interdisciplinary faculty combining engineering, informatics and life sciences - the audience that can hear "here is a forecasting benchmark and here is why the human baseline was missing" without either half needing translation
suggested_ask: Offer a guest session on time-series ML for glucose: the GlucoBench numbers, what a human scores against them, and the students play a round mid-lecture
notes: UPB publicly advertises free ML/AI and Data Science courses that include time-series forecasting and modelling - a natural host slot

name: UPT Timisoara - Machine Learning MSc (taught in English)
audience: MSc students in machine learning and predictive analysis
timing: Academic year
why_relevant: A whole MSc programme in ML and predictive analysis, taught in English. A real forecasting dataset with a human comparison arm is a guest lecture that gives them something they cannot download
suggested_ask: Guest lecture on evaluating time-series forecasters, using the study as the worked example, with the game as the first 15 minutes
notes: Same city as ws-umft-diabet and ws-medis-timisoara - Timisoara supports a three-stop trip

name: Babes-Bolyai University - Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science
audience: CS and maths students, summer-school participants
timing: Academic year; UBB hosted an AI summer school on climate extremes 22-24 June 2026
why_relevant: UBB already hosts AI summer schools on applying ML to time-series data in another domain, so the format is proven in the building. Same city as the strongest diabetes department in the file
suggested_ask: Guest lecture or a slot in a future summer school; approach in the same trip as Prof. Roman at UMF Cluj
notes: Cluj is the single highest-value trip in this file: UMF Cluj diabetes, UBB computer science, IT Days, the AI meetups and Noaptea Cercetatorilor all sit in one city

name: ASE Bucharest - Data Science International Summer School
audience: Students in data science and AI
timing: Annual summer school
why_relevant: A standing international summer school in data science - a recurring slot rather than a one-off event
suggested_ask: Ask to contribute a session on benchmarking time-series forecasters against human predictions
notes: Lower priority than UPB and UBB: no diabetes adjacency, and the audience is the least likely of the three to include CGM users

name: Congresul National al Societatii Romane de Diabet, Nutritie si Boli Metabolice
audience: Diabetologists, residents, GPs, related specialties
timing: Annual, May. 52nd edition 20-23 May 2026 at Timisoara Convention Centre. Next edition expected May 2027
why_relevant: The 2026 edition was themed "Diabetes in the era of TECH innovation and Artificial Intelligence" and its programme includes interactive workshops. A study measuring human versus model prediction is on-theme rather than adjacent, and the room is full of clinicians who each see hundreds of adults with CGMs
suggested_ask: Write to office@societate-diabet.ro about a workshop or e-poster for the next edition. The clinician ask is not "play this" but "tell your CGM patients the study exists"
notes: Cross-reference: srdnbm-ro in diabetes-orgs-catalogue.csv. The 52nd edition has passed - this row is a 2027 target. Verify the next edition's dates and city before drafting

name: FRDNBM - Federatia Romana de Diabet, Nutritie si Boli Metabolice
audience: Diabetes professionals and affiliated societies
timing: Rolling events calendar
why_relevant: Maintains a live events calendar for Romanian diabetes meetings, which is the cheapest way to find the smaller regional meetings that would actually take an unknown speaker
suggested_ask: Use the calendar as a source for this file rather than as a destination; ask about the smaller regional meetings
notes: Cross-reference: frdnbm-ro in diabetes-orgs-catalogue.csv, which notes an existing Romanian Academy collaboration

name: ASCOTID Mures - Asociatia Copiilor si Tinerilor Diabetici
audience: Children and young adults with type 1 diabetes, plus families
timing: Camps and educational workshops through the year
why_relevant: Already runs educational workshops and medical camps, so the format needs no explaining. The limit is age: the study is 18+, so only the young-adult tail and the accompanying adults can take part
suggested_ask: Offer the workshop for the over-18 members and the parents. Be explicit in the first message that under-18s can play for fun but cannot be enrolled
notes: Already in diabetes-orgs-catalogue.csv (ascotid-ro) and media-catalogue.csv (web-ascotid) - check what has already been sent before writing. Same city as ws-lstgm-targu-mures

name: Asociatia Medicala Sprijin pentru Diabet
audience: People with diabetes and their families
timing: Camps (Tabara Dulcineilor), World Diabetes Day, winter gathering
why_relevant: Runs a residential camp and has held its own conference series (Noi si Diabetul). A camp is the one setting where people have unhurried time to finish 6-12 rounds properly
suggested_ask: Ask whether an adult session can be added to a camp or a World Diabetes Day event
notes: Their programme leans paediatric and insulin-dependent children - confirm there is an adult audience before travelling. No contact details published on the pages fetched

name: ACES - Asociatia pentru Consiliere si Educatie in Sanatate
audience: General public, prevention and diabetes awareness
timing: World Diabetes Day period and prevention campaigns
why_relevant: Runs awareness and prevention actions aimed at people who do not yet have diabetes - which is the half of the sample that is hardest to reach through diabetes channels
suggested_ask: Offer a stand at a prevention event: a laptop, the game, and the printed souvenir for anyone who beats a threshold
notes: Found through rodiabet.ro coverage rather than an own site - locate the association's own page and contact before writing

name: Asociatia "Da, si eu pot!" - proiectul "Impreuna putem"
audience: Families of people with diabetes; doctors, psychologists, carers
timing: Project-based
why_relevant: Their project brings doctors, psychologists, patients and carers into the same room around lived experience. Carers of people with CGMs are adults who read traces daily and are eligible for the non-diabetic arm
suggested_ask: Offer a session for carers specifically - the people who read someone else's trace and guess what comes next
notes: Listed through CASPA, the Romanian patient-association community. Smallest and least verified row in the patient block

name: Ziua Mondiala a Diabetului - Romanian events, 14 November
audience: Mixed: patients, clinicians, general public
timing: 14 November every year. Romanian associations run stands, free courses, roundtables and workshops around that date
why_relevant: Not a venue but the date every Romanian diabetes organisation already has an event on. It is far easier to be added to someone's existing 14 November programme than to ask them to create an event
suggested_ask: Pick two or three of the patient organisations in this file and ask each, by September, to add a play-the-study table to their 14 November programme
notes: 14 November 2026 is seven weeks after this file was written - too late for a headline slot, realistic for a table. Treat 2027 as the properly planned run

name: IT Days
audience: 800+ developers and tech professionals; AI and hands-on lab tracks
timing: 11-12 November 2026 at Cluj Innovation Park; annual, November
why_relevant: Its published structure includes hands-on labs and an AI domain alongside research. A room of 800 technical adults is a recruitment pool for the non-diabetic arm and a plausible source of people who would argue with the benchmark, which is useful
suggested_ask: Propose a hands-on lab: play the game, then look at what the ML models score on the same segments. If the CFP has closed, ask for a table in the community area instead
notes: Nearest large event to the date this file was written. No CFP or contact email exposed on the front page - use the site's contact form. Same city as UMF Cluj and UBB

name: DevTalks Romania (Bucharest and Cluj editions)
audience: 2500+ developers per edition; AI, ML, DeepTech and Data topics
timing: Bucharest June, Cluj September. The 2026 Cluj edition was 24 September 2026
why_relevant: The largest tech conference in the country and it runs a public Sessionize call for speakers, so there is an actual door rather than a contact form
suggested_ask: Submit a talk through Sessionize for the next edition: a forecasting benchmark where the baseline is a person's hand, and what we learned building it
notes: A stage talk suits the ML-teaching half of the offer but not the play-and-print half - a conference stage is the wrong shape for handing out souvenirs. Consider combining with a booth

name: DevCon Romania
audience: Developers; dedicated AI and Machine Learning track
timing: November
why_relevant: Has a standing AI and ML track and a public call for speakers
suggested_ask: Same talk as DevTalks, submitted through Sessionize
notes: Lowest-effort submission in the file because the CFP is public. Low expected recruitment yield - a stage talk converts worse than a played round

name: EEML - Eastern European Machine Learning Summer School
audience: Graduate students and researchers in ML
timing: Annual, summer. 2026 edition 27 July - 1 August in Cetinje, Montenegro
why_relevant: The successor to the Transylvanian Machine Learning Summer School, which started in Cluj. Its alumni and organiser network is the shortest path to Romanian ML researchers who could critique or use the benchmark
suggested_ask: Not a workshop venue - approach it as a place to find collaborators and to ask whether a practical session on human-versus-model forecasting would fit a future edition
notes: tmlss.ro now redirects to the EEML identity. The school moves country each year, so it is only a Romanian venue in some editions

name: Cluj AI and data meetups (Cluj Data & AI, Artificial Intelligence Cluj)
audience: Local ML and data practitioners, tens to low hundreds per event
timing: Monthly-ish, year-round
why_relevant: A meetup organiser can say yes in a week, where a conference takes a year. Good place to run the lecture once and find out which parts of it land before proposing it to a congress
suggested_ask: Offer a 30-minute talk plus a live play session. Bring souvenirs - a meetup is small enough that everyone who plays gets one
notes: Also: https://www.meetup.com/artificial-intelligence-cluj/ and https://www.meetup.com/big-data-data-science-meetup-cluj-napoca/ . Fastest route in the file from ask to stage

name: Bucharest AI and ML meetups (Bucharest.AI, Bucharest Machine Learning Applications)
audience: Local ML practitioners, academia and industry
timing: Monthly, year-round
why_relevant: Bucharest Machine Learning Applications runs monthly and explicitly brings in outside speakers. Members come from academia, industry and the hobbyist edge
suggested_ask: Same offer as Cluj: talk plus live play, souvenirs for everyone who finishes a session
notes: Also: https://www.meetup.com/bucharest-ai/ , https://www.meetup.com/bucharest-deep-learning/ , https://www.meetup.com/artificial-intelligence-bucharest/ . AI Romania (airomania.eu) runs a Slack that spans these communities

name: Noaptea Cercetatorilor Europeni (European Researchers' Night)
audience: General public of all ages, thousands per city
timing: One night each September. 2026 edition Friday 25 September, 13:00-23:00
why_relevant: The programme already includes 3D printing and robotics stands next to medical ones, and it runs for ten hours in a public space. A stand with two laptops and a bowl of printed souvenirs is exactly the native format here, and it is free to the public so the crowd is broad
suggested_ask: Apply to the Cluj organising consortium for a stand in the 2027 edition. For 2026 it is too late to register - go and watch how the stands are run instead
notes: The single best format fit in this file: public, all-evening, hands-on, and the souvenir table is already the local idiom. Caveat: a large part of the crowd is under 18 and cannot be enrolled - they can still play, and their parents can enrol

name: Romanian Science Festival (RSF Caravan)
city: Rural and small-town Romania (Maramures, Arges and others)
audience: School pupils and their teachers, thousands per caravan
timing: Caravan format, three-hour events across several localities
why_relevant: Founded to bring science to rural and small-town Romania through the academic diaspora - a Romanian researcher working abroad is precisely the mentor profile they recruit. Their workshop menu already lists AI and medicine
suggested_ask: Apply as an RSF mentor with the game as the workshop. Be clear that the value here is outreach and future recruitment, not enrolment: most participants are under 18
notes: Do not count this as recruitment. The study is 18+, and the RSF audience is school pupils. It earns its place as the clearest expression of why the game exists, plus teacher contacts

name: Bucharest Science Festival
audience: General public, students, families
timing: Annual, multi-day
why_relevant: Described in Romanian press as the country's most important science and technology festival - an urban adult audience alongside the family one
suggested_ask: Apply with a workshop for the adult strand; ask which sessions are adults-only before proposing
notes: Check whether the adult-audience strand actually exists before applying - the value of this row depends entirely on it

name: Nod Makerspace
audience: Makers, designers, engineers; adults
timing: Runs its own public events, courses and fairs year-round
why_relevant: The one venue in this file where the 3D-printed souvenir is not a curiosity but the house language - they have the printers. An evening where people play, and the prize prints while they watch, is a stronger version of the conference format
suggested_ask: Propose a public evening: play the study, and print the winners' souvenirs live on their machines
notes: Splaiul Unirii 160, in the former Cotton Factory. Also a route to Romanian maker communities in other cities if the evening works

name: Pint of Science
audience: Adults in pubs and cafes
timing: Three evenings each May, worldwide
why_relevant: Format-perfect for this study - adults, phones in hand, in a pub, three nights a year - but Romanian press reported in 2026 that Romania is not on the festival map
suggested_ask: Either join a team in a country where it runs, or ask the organisation what starting a Romanian city involves. Neither is a quick win
notes: Romania's absence was reported by edupedu.ro in 2026. Kept in the file because the format matches so exactly that founding a local edition is worth considering, not because it is actionable now
